svg.text: Глава 15 · Протоколы транспортного уровня TCP и UDP
Олифер, 7-е изд. · RAG p0442:c01–p0471:c01 · PDF 442–471 · printed 441–470
1 · Application demultiplexing
Transport layer maps host traffic to application ports
Socket source model → IP address + TCP/UDP port
TCP connection → pair of endpoint sockets
One server socket can participate in many distinct connections
Source port-range model is simplified and recorded as an edition boundary
2 · UDP vs TCP service
UDP → message-oriented datagrams · 8-byte header · best effort
UDP checksum detects corruption but does not repair delivery
TCP → unstructured duplex byte stream over unreliable IP
SYN/ACK/FIN/RST plus sequence/ACK/window state build reliability
TCP segmentation is independent of application message boundaries
3 · ARQ and sliding-window progression
Stop-and-Wait → simplest ACK/timeout/retry, low utilization
Go-Back-N → send window + cumulative ACK + tail retransmission
Selective Repeat → receive buffer + individual ACK/timer + selective resend
TCP adopts a byte-oriented window and cumulative contiguous ACK semantics
SACK selectively confirms out-of-order received ranges in source extension model
Reliability consumes buffers, timers and connection state
4 · Flow control and retransmission timing
rwnd advertises receiver buffer capacity
Zero window stops ordinary sending until receiver capacity returns
Sent-but-unacknowledged data remains in retransmission storage
RTO must track changing RTT: too short → spurious resend; too long → stalls
Source presents adaptive RTT averaging as the timing principle
Exact modern estimator/defaults are deliberately not inferred
5 · Congestion control
flow control → protect receiver
congestion control → protect network
cwnd is sender-controlled; effective send window constrained by rwnd and cwnd
Slow Start → exponential growth, threshold → slower growth in source example
Three duplicate ACKs / ECN can signal congestion or loss before timeout
6 · TCP evolves beyond the classical model
SACK → selective loss recovery
CUBIC / BBR / HyStart++ → alternative performance/congestion approaches
Westwood+ → source-described wireless-oriented variant
MPTCP → several subflows/interfaces under one logical connection
RFC/default/deployment claims in the table remain edition snapshots
Operational reading rule
TCP failure → socket pair → handshake/state → seq/ACK continuity → rwnd → RTO/retransmissions → congestion/ECN.
UDP failure → socket → datagram emission/arrival/checksum → application-level semantics.
No executable OS tuning or packet-capture command is supplied by the chapter.
Chapter 16 starts at p0472:c01 · reading state unchanged · source findings recorded separately.
